steps.title: Key Principle
steps.body: The body needs energy (in the form of ATP - adenosine triphosphate) to fuel muscle contraction. This energy is released by breaking down fuel stores. Depending on the intensity and duration of exercise, the body uses different energy systems.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Aerobic exercise is exercise performed "with oxygen." It uses the aerobic energy system, which breaks down glucose using oxygen to release energy. This is the main energy system for low-to-moderate intensity, long-duration activities.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Anaerobic exercise is exercise performed "without oxygen." It uses the anaerobic energy system, which breaks down glucose without oxygen to release energy quickly. This is the main system for high-intensity, short-duration activities.

steps.title: ATP-PC (Alactic) System
steps.body: The immediate energy system for very short, explosive efforts (0-10 seconds). Uses stored phosphocreatine (PC) in the muscles to resynthesise ATP without producing lactic acid. It is called "alactic" because no lactic acid is produced.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Write the word equation for aerobic respiration. | Write the word equation for anaerobic respiration. | Explain why a marathon runner uses primarily the aerobic system while a 100m sprinter uses primarily the anaerobic system.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Memorise both word equations - they are frequently tested (4-6 marks) Always explain EPOC in terms of what the extra oxygen is used FOR Know the difference between alactic (ATP-PC, 0-10 sec) and lactic (glycolytic, 10 sec-2 min) systems When comparing aerobic vs anaerobic, use a table format in your answer Active recovery is always preferred over passive - explain WHY (blood flow, oxygen delivery) Lactic acid causes fatigue - always mention this when discussing the anaerobic system
